summary: multipass is a password manager for one person: today a single age file encrypted under one passphrase, and, once the plans in the pull request beneath this one ship, a package (a folder of files that are written once and never changed) whose files a random vault key encrypts. This pull request adds a plan, and no code, for letting several people share one package, such as a household's recovery codes.
The plan keeps every entry under the symmetric vault key and uses public-key cryptography only to hand each new vault key to each member:

1. Each member has an identity. It is an age hybrid post-quantum key pair, ML-KEM-768 with X25519 (age's mlkem768x25519 recipient type), kept in the package in identity.<member>.age under that member's own passphrase.
  2. Each new vault key goes out as grants. Whoever rotates the key writes one grant.<gen>.<member>.age per member, encrypted to that member's public recipient.
  3. The member list is inside the store. A new store format 4 adds member records beside entries, so the plan expects only vault-key holders to change who gets the next key.
  4. Joining needs a fingerprint read aloud. A newcomer writes a plaintext join request, and a member admits them after both read the same fingerprint out of band.
  5. Removal means leaving someone out of the next rotation. The removal rotation does not carry the old key forward, and the plan lists what a removed member keeps.
The plan is a draft at priority later, and nothing in it is scheduled. Its seven open questions, including hand-written cryptography against Apple's CryptoKit, are deferred on purpose.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Vault key: the random 256-bit key that encrypts the store files, from the vault-key plan. It rotates at least every 21 days.
  • Generation: one vault key and the files written under it, named by a random id.
  • Identity and recipient: a member's private and public key in age's terms.
  • Grant: one generation's key file text, encrypted to one member's recipient.
  • Tombstone: the dated marker a removed record leaves so a merge does not bring it back, from the mergeable-store plan.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
The Projector review of 492d0bc requested changes, with four open threads:

  • Forged and replayed grants (P1): grants are not authenticated, so anyone who knows a recipient can plant a vault key, and a removed member can get back in.
  • Rule documents (P2): the plan reverses AGENTS.md and README.md rules without a changes-by-file section.
  • passwd (P2): changing a passphrase keeps the same identity, so it no longer locks out someone who learned the old one.
  • Format 4 (P2): a member record looks like an entry named member ….

It also lists five suggestions in the review body.

groups.title: The shared-vaults plan
groups.kicker: One new plan document, read against the plans and rule documents it builds on
intro: The whole change is one plan, docs/projects/shared-vaults/readme.md. Sections 2.1 to 2.5 lay out the package's new files, how a member opens the vault, the member list, joining and removing, and what removal cannot undo. Section 2.7 weighs about 1,500 lines of new constant-time cryptography in src/crypto against calling CryptoKit, and section 3 explains the rejected alternatives.

Read it beside the plans it depends on, all in this stack: the mergeable store (store format 3 and Store::merge, where the newest modified stamp wins), the vault key (the package, key files, and rotation), and session unlock (an agent that holds the vault key). AGENTS.md and README.md matter too, because they currently describe multipass as single-user, passphrase-only, and without sharing.

files.note: The new plan: package layout, opening, the member list in format 4, membership, removal, implementation choices, and open questions.

checks.text: § 2.3 claims only a vault-key holder can change who gets the key, but grants are unauthenticated public-key encryption. A sync service that saw a join request, or a removed member, can write a grant with a key of its own and a store file that adds itself, and the next open adopts it. A removed member can also replay an old grant. Open review thread (P1).

Public-key grants reverse AGENTS.md's passphrase-only and single-user rules and README.md's no-sharing and no-public-keys claims, and the plan has no changes-by-file section saying how they change. Open review thread (P2).

The plan never says what passwd does in a shared vault. Re-encrypting the identity file keeps the same identity, so an old passphrase and an old copy of the file still open every later grant. Open review thread (P2).
A member <id> line has the same shape as an entry named member …, which entry names allow today, and § 2.3 gives Store::from_text no rule to tell them apart. Open review thread (P2).
§ 6 defers every question on purpose: the user owns 1 to 5, and the implementer owns 6 and 7. A draft plan claims no readiness, so these do not block review.
